title: Usage forecasting for the current period
summary: Projected end-of-period usage per customer and meter, with a confidence band, in the usage page and the API. Beta: the model and the API shape may change.
body:
Forecasting projects each customer's end-of-period quantity per meter from the last 28 days of hourly roll-ups (story method). Projections appear on customer usage pages and at GET /v1/customers/{id}/forecast.

Known limits in this beta

  • New customers need 7 days of data before a projection is shown
  • Seasonality beyond weekly cycles is not modeled yet
  • The response field band will be renamed interval before GA

Feedback: reply to the beta email for this build.

title: Credit burndown on every invoice
summary: Invoices now print the credit balance before and after the period, and the customer usage page shows a burndown chart rendered on the server.
body:
Each invoice now carries a credits section: opening balance, consumed this period by grant, expired, and closing balance. The same numbers appear in the invoice explain export.

The customer usage page shows a server-rendered burndown chart for the current commitment term.

Also in v4.12

  • Rate card diff view between two versions
  • Webhook retries now back off up to 24 hours

title: Contract-aware rating
summary: Rate usage against a customer's contract — ramps, mid-term amendments and minimum commitments — instead of a plan-level rate card. Second beta build.
body:
Contract-aware rating lets a single customer's contract define its own rate schedule: ramp deals (year 1 at one rate, year 2 at another), mid-term amendments that take effect on a date, and true-up of minimum commitments at term end.

Changed since beta.1

  • Amendments can now be back-dated within an open period
  • True-up lines show the commitment shortfall as its own explain tree

Do not use yet for

  • Multi-currency contracts
  • Contracts with more than 12 ramp steps

title: Late-event window is now per meter
summary: Set a different late-event window for each meter — 72 hours for API calls, 7 days for a partner's daily file drops — instead of one window per account.
body:
Windows can now be set per meter. Partner file drops often need days; API meters rarely need more than hours. Closing earlier where you can means invoices go out sooner.

Existing accounts keep their account-wide window as the default for every meter.

title: Invoice explain export to CSV and JSON
summary: Download the full explain tree for an invoice — every line, every dimension, event counts — as CSV or JSON, from the UI or the API.
body: Auditors and large customers asked for the explain tree outside the UI. The export includes one row per line per dimension value, with event counts, duplicates, late events and the rate card version.

title: Fix: duplicate counts on batches split across midnight UTC
summary: Batches whose events straddled midnight UTC could show duplicates dropped on the wrong day in explain trees. Totals were always correct; the day split now is too.
body: Only the per-day display in explain trees was affected. Rated quantities and invoice totals were correct throughout. Explain trees for affected invoices were regenerated automatically.

title: Unique-count meters for active-device pricing
summary: New aggregation: unique(field) counts distinct values per period, for pricing per active device, seat-free MAU or distinct API key.
body: Unique-count meters count distinct values of a field over the billing period, computed exactly (not estimated) up to 50 million distinct values per customer per period (story limit).
